notes: S015.check1 (main-reader targeted counterexample): as written without a rank or nonabelian restriction, the Corollaire includes the free profinite group F on one generator, taking the open subgroup to be F itself. Every finite quotient of F is cyclic, so F is abelian; the defining universal property supplies a quotient of order two, so F is nontrivial. Hence C_F(F)=F is not {1}. The assertion that a free profinite group has trivial centre cannot hold in this generality. This is a check of the literal unrestricted statement, not a claim about a more restricted geometric situation that the author may have intended. The source wording and its two à vérifier notes remain unchanged.

S015.check2 (conditional refinement, checked): if G is torsion-free and has a normal subgroup U of finite index with Z(U)={1}, then C_G(U)={1}. Indeed C_G(U) injects into G/U by the kernel computation C_G(U) intersect U=Z(U), so it is finite; a torsion-free group has no nontrivial finite subgroup. This isolates the two premises needed by the written final argument without asserting that the manuscript has established them. No unprinted rank hypothesis has been inserted.
